style.register: 游戏指南体，简体中文，简洁直陈，不用敬语，不用『您』。
style.numbers: 数字、百分比、游戏内数值原样保留（如 10%、+5%）。
style.placeholders: ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ 等占位符必须原样保留且不得增删、不得调换顺序；它们代表图标或链接。
style.markup: 不要输出 HTML 标签；保留原文的换行与项目符号结构。
style.properNouns: 国家、人物、舰名等专有名词使用通用中文译名（如 German Reich → 德意志国，Adolf Hitler → 阿道夫·希特勒）；Paradox 未汉化的专有名词可保留英文并加中文注释。
style.consistency: 同一英文术语在全站必须使用同一译名。

The below is ⟦0⟧ player suggested strategies for ⟦1⟧. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.

In 1936, Japan can release ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ as ⟦4⟧ without losing any core territory. Palau must be released before Micronesia. These puppets have the ⟦5⟧, with which they can provide additional factories. However, countries with the generic focus tree are programmed not to begin industrial focuses until 1939 if they have only one state, so Taiwan and Palau will be of limited use as puppets until then.

⟦0⟧ is by far the strongest nation in East Asia when it comes to military strength and has plenty of options for expanding its sphere of influence. That being said, Japan suffers from a chronic lack of resources, given the size of its military, and will, as it realized in real life, become very dependent on trade to fuel its war machine unless the problem is properly addressed.

Japan starts the game with a total of 54 factories (16 military, 24 civilian and 14 naval dockyards) which is comparable to most of the other major nations and this gives Japan the biggest industrial capacity in East Asia.

The Imperial Japanese army consists of a rather colorful mix of units, ranging from Regular to Green in experience and with varying levels of equipment. Many of the division templates are also somewhat questionable when it comes to composition. A lot of rearming and reorganizing will be needed in order to bring up the military to par with the other major powers.

The Imperial Japanese Navy is the third-largest navy in the world and the largest one in East Asia. Because Japan is an island nation and also controls a large matrix of smaller islands throughout the pacific ocean, the navy will be vital to ensure that the Japanese Empire remains properly connected and that supply lines remain open. As such, Japan will need to build up its naval dockyard capacity in order to allow it to expand its naval force and replace lost ships.
